key_insight: Detonation spraying parameters can be tuned to control titanium dioxide-based coating roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity, with clear optimal settings for maximum water repellency.
engineering_relevance: The reported scaling laws and predictive equations can guide process selection in coating production to target surface finish and functional wetting behavior.
method: Varied detonation spraying process conditions, especially nozzle passage speed and spray distance.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle to quantify surface characteristics.
Derived empirical relationships linking process parameters to surface properties, including inverse power and parabolic dependencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental observation and model fitting of coating roughness, thickness, and contact angle versus process parameters, leading to optimized hydrophobicity conditions.
watch_item: The relationships appear empirical and may be specific to the studied materials and spraying setup, so transferability to other systems should be validated.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
